items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: And I met Wallace Davenport, a black trumpeter who was pretty hot in New Orleans, and ended up doing two albums with him and would go down to New Orleans and sit in with him.

ctx.x: I know. I mean you know so I told Dean, when he asked me, and if anybody asks me, I’d played like the Mississippi Jazz Festival or something back home, but nobody there. So I got to meet these guys and a lot of Washington, DC players as well that I’ve remained

friends with for years. But I’m thinking God dang this is unbelievable. And it was. I mean Lou McGarrity. And I met Wallace Davenport, a black trumpeter who was pretty hot in New Orleans, and ended up doing two albums with him and would go down to New Orleans and sit in with him. You know I couldn’t sign on because he was on a small club group. But that was the biggest door that anybody had ever opened for me. Well later on Dean was sick and he was in the hospital here in Orlando. And he was terminal, the word…
What do you do in that situation, or maybe later, if you got on the bandstand and someone calls a tune and everybody knows it but you?
